This is game 146 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.

# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))
# Usage: python3 count.py <<'EOF' ...board rows 9..1 pasted from the board output... EOF
# Area count of the CURRENT position: stones + empty regions touching only one colour.
# Empty regions touching both colours are printed as "open" (count for nobody yet).
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
score={"X":0,"O":0}
for p in B:
    if B[p] in "XO": score[B[p]]+=1
seen=set();open_pts=[]
for p in B:
    if B[p]=='.' and p not in seen:
        g=[p];seen.add(p);k=0;touch=set()
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.' and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
                elif B[q] in "XO": touch.add(B[q])
            k+=1
        if len(touch)==1: score[touch.pop()]+=len(g)
        else: open_pts+=g
print("Black",score["X"],"White",score["O"],"+7 komi =",score["O"]+7,"open",len(open_pts))
print("open:",",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in open_pts)))

## Game 144 — White vs 10k — resigned at move 32 (~20 area)
Moves: B G7, C4, B D5 (shoulder hit), G3, B D4, D3 (hane), B C3 crosscut, B3 (atari),

B J2 -> G1-G3-H2 in atari (H1), black chain connected out via F4. Resigned.
Takeaways:
- Black sacrificed 3 corner stones; every black move there (C5, B5) built a wall
  B5-D5-D4-E4 while my 7 moves made an ~18-pt corner. Then the wall + G4 cap killed G3.
- vs D5 shoulder hit on C4: answer it locally (C5/D4) at move 4, not G3.
- Lone 3rd-line stone vs attach (F3) + cap (G4): secure the corner side (H3/H2) first;
  black's F2-F1 slide then left G1-G3 with libs H1/H2 only vs black's escape at F4.

## Game 145 — Black vs 12k — resigned at move 35 (~34 vs 47+7)
Moves: C4, W D7, G6, W G7 (attach on top), F6, W F7, E6, W G3 (invasion), H4, W D3,
F3 (wedge), W F2 (hane under), E3, W E2 (E3-F3 at 2 libs), E4, W H3, D4, W C3, B3,
W C2, B2, W B1, H2?, W J2, A1, W C1, D1, W D2, G2, W G1! (G2-H2 atari) -> W bottom
B1-J1/row 2 alive (~20). E7 wedge, W E8, D6, W C7. Resigned.
Takeaways:
- G6 + F6 + E6 gave W the whole top (rows 7-9 = 27) for 3 W stones; I let W build a
  row-7 wall on MY moves. With W top = 27, W needs only 11 more: one living invasion
  under my rows 4-6 = loss. Playing solid on row 6 vs W G7 attach is too slow.
- vs W G3 invasion (my strength: C4, row-6 wall): H4 then F3 wedge between W D3 and
  G3 was the wrong fight. W F2/E2 hane-under made my F3-E3 2 libs and W crawled row 2.
  Every W stone sat on row 2-3 and the whole bottom row became W's eye space.
  Better: answer G3 from UNDER/the side with room (F2/E2 low, or G4 + E3 low pincer)
  and keep my own stones at 3+ libs; don't wedge between two W low stones from above.
- Reading: a placement (H2) next to W's G3-H3 with W J2 coming = W G2/G1 atari wins;
  the G2 cut only works if W can't atari it from G1. Read W's ATARI replies first.

That means my E3 group has liberties at D3 and E2, while F2-F3 only has E2 and F1 — I'm checking whether black playing E2 next could threaten to connect or cut these groups further.

C4 is in real danger with only two liberties, so I need to extend either toward D4 (giving B4, D5, D3) or toward B4 (giving A4, B3, B5, D4, a safer four liberties), though black sealing with D4 afterward still leaves my group pressured. Alternatively, cutting at E3 to attack the weak F2-F3 group looks promising — if black defends with E2, I can extend to D3 and start chasing that group toward atari, though I need to watch whether black's D4 response also threatens C4 simultaneously.

Trying B3 to pressure C3's liberties toward capture, though it tangles my B4-C4-B3 group against black's C3, C5. events.text:
I lost game 146: I resigned as White against the 12k opponent at move 28.

**What happened:** Black opened at tengen (E5) and then played C5 on top of my C4. I didn't answer C5 and played G6 on the other side, then F4. That left me with two weak areas at once:
- Black cut F4 off from G6 with F5 and pressed it (E4, F3, F2), so my right group was forced into slow, solid moves.
- Black then attacked the C4 stone from below with C3. I extended B4, B3, B2, and Black's B1 hane took the bottom-left corner, the group's only eye space.
- I tried to escape through D4 and D5, but Black's D6 and B6 shut that down. My six-stone left group was left with three liberties, all on the A column, and no way to make two eyes.

Even if I had won the whole right side, my area would have been about 28 points. With komi that is still well short of the 38 White needs, so I resigned.

**Notes saved for next session:**
- **`games.md`:** a Game 146 entry with the full move list and what I took from it.
- **`CLAUDE.md`, lesson #92:**
  - Against tengen plus C5 on my C4, answer locally at move 4 (B5 hane under or D5 hane at the head) instead of playing elsewhere.
  - Don't add a 4th-line stone like F4 toward tengen while C4 is still weak.
  - When a group is caught between C5 above and C3 below, consider D3/D4 before crawling along the B column.
- **Ladder status:** this was a second loss in a row at 12k, so the notes set game 147 to Black against 14k. The record now reads 27-44-3 as White and 13-29-1 against 12k.
